AI Assistants.reasoning: Genie for natural language data queries, AI/BI Dashboards with AI-generated insights, and Databricks Assistant for code generation and debugging across notebooks and SQL.

OLTP Databases.reasoning: Databricks is an analytics platform, not designed for OLTP workloads. Customers use separate databases for transactional applications.

Data Platform.reasoning: Unified lakehouse platform combining data warehouse and data lake. Native support for all workloads—ETL, BI, ML, and AI—on a single platform with Delta Lake.

DS/ML Platform.reasoning: Comprehensive ML platform with MLflow, Feature Store, Model Serving, AutoML, and Unity Catalog for ML artifacts. Best-in-class experiment tracking and model deployment.

GenAI/Agent Platform.reasoning: Complete GenAI stack with Mosaic AI for training/fine-tuning, Vector Search, Model Serving with Foundation Model APIs, and Agent Framework for building AI applications.

Data Warehouse/Lakehouse.reasoning: Photon-powered SQL analytics with serverless compute. Industry-leading price-performance for data warehousing with Delta Lake open format.

Data Eng (Ingest, ETL, Streaming).reasoning: Apache Spark for batch, Structured Streaming for real-time. Delta Live Tables for declarative ETL. Auto Loader for incremental ingestion. LakeFlow for managed pipelines.

Orchestration.reasoning: Databricks Workflows for native orchestration with multi-task jobs, dependencies, and monitoring. Integrates with Airflow and other tools.

BI & Agentic BI.reasoning: AI/BI product with Genie for natural language queries and dashboards. Direct lake access for sub-second queries. Integrates with major BI tools.

DS/ML.reasoning: Full ML lifecycle: experiments, Feature Store, model registry, AutoML, and serverless Model Serving. MLflow integration for tracking and reproducibility.

Gen AI & Agents Dev.reasoning: Mosaic AI for training custom LLMs, Foundation Model APIs, Vector Search, RAG applications, and Agent Framework for building compound AI systems.

Apps Hosting.reasoning: Databricks Apps for hosting Streamlit, Gradio, and custom web apps directly on the platform. Newer capability, still maturing compared to dedicated PaaS.

Open Table Storage.reasoning: Delta Lake creator and primary contributor. UniForm provides interoperability with Iceberg and Hudi. Open format by design.

Catalog & Governance.reasoning: Unity Catalog provides unified governance for data, ML models, and AI assets. Fine-grained access control, lineage, and data discovery across the lakehouse.

AI Assistants.reasoning: Cortex Analyst for natural language SQL queries. Copilot features in Snowsight for code assistance. Less comprehensive than Databricks Genie/Assistant.

OLTP Databases.reasoning: Snowflake is OLAP only. Not designed for transactional workloads. Hybrid tables provide limited OLTP-like features but not a replacement for OLTP databases.

Data Platform.reasoning: Strong data warehousing but limited native data engineering. Relies on partners for ETL. No native streaming—requires Snowpipe or external tools.

DS/ML Platform.reasoning: Snowpark ML for in-Snowflake ML with stored procedures. Limited compared to Databricks—no native experiment tracking or model registry. Feature Store recently added.

GenAI/Agent Platform.reasoning: Cortex AI for LLMs with functions like COMPLETE and EMBED. Arctic LLM for text-to-SQL. Lacks agent framework and comprehensive AI development platform.

Data Warehouse/Lakehouse.reasoning: Industry-leading cloud data warehouse with instant elasticity. Iceberg Tables for lakehouse patterns. Excellent for structured data analytics.

Data Eng (Ingest, ETL, Streaming).reasoning: Snowpipe for micro-batch ingestion, Dynamic Tables for transformations. No native streaming—recently acquired Streamlit for UI but not for streaming data.

Orchestration.reasoning: Tasks and DAGs for basic orchestration. Less sophisticated than dedicated orchestration tools. Many customers use external orchestrators.

BI & Agentic BI.reasoning: Native dashboards and visualizations in Snowsight. Acquired Streamlit for apps. Cortex for NL queries. Less mature BI than Power BI or Tableau integrations.

DS/ML.reasoning: Snowpark ML for model training in Snowflake. Model Registry added recently. No native MLflow, limited experiment tracking compared to Databricks.

Gen AI & Agents Dev.reasoning: Cortex AI with LLM functions and Arctic model. Vector embedding support. No agent framework, no model fine-tuning, limited to pre-built functions.

Apps Hosting.reasoning: Streamlit in Snowflake for data apps. Native Apps Framework for distributing applications. Strong app development story post-Streamlit acquisition.

Open Table Storage.reasoning: Iceberg Tables (native Iceberg support) enable open format storage. Supports reading external Iceberg tables. Moving toward open formats but historically proprietary.

Catalog & Governance.reasoning: Horizon for governance with data classification, access control, lineage, and data quality. Comprehensive governance for Snowflake-managed data.

subPlatforms.name: Azure Data Products
subPlatforms.description: Azure Synapse, Data Factory, Event Hubs

subPlatforms.name: Microsoft Foundry
subPlatforms.description: Unified AI platform (formerly Azure AI Foundry)

AI Assistants.reasoning: Copilot deeply integrated across all Microsoft products—M365, Power BI, Data Factory, Azure. Natural language for report creation, pipeline building, and code generation.

OLTP Databases.reasoning: Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, PostgreSQL Flexible Server handle transactional workloads. Strong OLTP options as separate Azure services.

Data Platform.reasoning: Unified SaaS platform combining data lake, warehouse, data engineering, and analytics. OneLake provides single data copy across all workloads.

DS/ML Platform.reasoning: Synapse ML and notebooks for data science. Azure ML integration for full MLOps. Less native than Databricks—requires switching to Azure ML for production ML.

GenAI/Agent Platform.reasoning: Microsoft Foundry provides unified AI platform with OpenAI and Anthropic models. Copilot Studio for agent building. Agent Factory combines Work IQ, Fabric IQ, and Foundry IQ.

Data Warehouse/Lakehouse.reasoning: Synapse Data Warehouse for analytics. Lakehouse with Delta Lake format. Direct Lake mode for fast Power BI queries without data movement.

Data Eng (Ingest, ETL, Streaming).reasoning: Data Factory for ETL/ELT, Spark notebooks for transformations, Dataflows Gen2 for low-code. Eventstream for real-time ingestion.

Orchestration.reasoning: Data Factory pipelines for orchestration with triggers, dependencies, and monitoring. Integrates with Azure DevOps and GitHub for CI/CD.

BI & Agentic BI.reasoning: Power BI is the core BI tool—industry leader in enterprise BI. Copilot for natural language report creation. Direct Lake for real-time lakehouse BI.

DS/ML.reasoning: Notebooks with Spark ML. For production ML, typically requires Azure ML integration. No native Feature Store or MLflow-equivalent in Fabric.

Gen AI & Agents Dev.reasoning: Microsoft Foundry with OpenAI and Anthropic models. Copilot Studio for low-code agents. Agent Factory for enterprise agent development.

Apps Hosting.reasoning: Power Apps for low-code apps. No native Streamlit/Gradio equivalent in Fabric. Custom apps require Azure App Service separately.

Open Table Storage.reasoning: OneLake uses Delta Lake/Parquet as the native format. Supports shortcuts to external Delta and Iceberg tables for interoperability.

Catalog & Governance.reasoning: Microsoft Purview integration for governance, lineage, and data discovery. OneLake provides unified data access layer with centralized security policies.

AI Assistants.reasoning: Amazon Q for AWS console assistance, Q in QuickSight for BI, CodeWhisperer for development. Strong in-product AI across AWS services.

OLTP Databases.reasoning: RDS (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server), Aurora, DynamoDB. Comprehensive OLTP database options from relational to NoSQL.

Data Platform.reasoning: Broad services but fragmented—Redshift, EMR, Glue, Athena are separate products. Requires significant integration work for unified experience.

DS/ML Platform.reasoning: SageMaker is comprehensive ML platform with notebooks, training, deployment, Feature Store, and MLOps. Strong enterprise ML capabilities.

GenAI/Agent Platform.reasoning: Bedrock provides managed access to foundation models (Claude, Llama, Titan). Agents for Bedrock for building AI agents. Strong but less integrated than Databricks.

Data Warehouse/Lakehouse.reasoning: Redshift for data warehouse, Redshift Serverless for flexibility. S3 Tables for Iceberg lakehouse. Strong but multiple products to manage.

Data Eng (Ingest, ETL, Streaming).reasoning: Glue for ETL, EMR for Spark, Kinesis for streaming, MSK for Kafka. Comprehensive but requires stitching multiple services together.

Orchestration.reasoning: Step Functions for workflow orchestration, MWAA (managed Airflow), EventBridge for event-driven. Multiple options available.

BI & Agentic BI.reasoning: QuickSight for BI with Q for natural language queries. Less market share than Power BI or Tableau. Agentic BI features emerging.

DS/ML.reasoning: SageMaker provides full ML lifecycle—notebooks, training, hyperparameter tuning, deployment, Feature Store, and monitoring.

Gen AI & Agents Dev.reasoning: Bedrock for foundation models, Agents for Bedrock, Knowledge Bases for RAG. PartyRock for no-code experimentation. Comprehensive GenAI offering.

Apps Hosting.reasoning: Lambda, ECS, EKS, App Runner, Elastic Beanstalk. AWS has the most comprehensive app hosting options across serverless, containers, and PaaS.

Open Table Storage.reasoning: S3 Tables provides native Iceberg support. Historically proprietary formats. Increasing open format adoption but Databricks leads here.

Catalog & Governance.reasoning: Glue Data Catalog, Lake Formation for access control. Governance features exist but spread across services. Less unified than Unity Catalog.

subPlatforms.name: Vertex AI

subPlatforms.name: Gemini for Enterprise
subPlatforms.description: Gemini across Google Workspace and Cloud

AI Assistants.reasoning: Gemini integrated across Google Cloud console, BigQuery, Looker, and Colab. Strong code assistance, SQL generation, and data exploration agents.

OLTP Databases.reasoning: Cloud SQL (MySQL, PostgreSQL), Cloud Spanner for global scale, Firestore for NoSQL, Bigtable for wide-column. Excellent OLTP options.

Data Platform.reasoning: BigQuery-centric with Dataproc, Dataflow, Pub/Sub as supporting services. Not as unified as Databricks or Fabric—requires service integration.

DS/ML Platform.reasoning: Vertex AI is comprehensive ML platform with AutoML, custom training, Feature Store, Model Registry, and managed notebooks. Strong MLOps capabilities.

GenAI/Agent Platform.reasoning: Vertex AI with Gemini models, Agent Builder, Agent Development Kit (ADK), and Agent2Agent protocol. 20x increase in Vertex AI usage driven by Gemini adoption.

Data Warehouse/Lakehouse.reasoning: BigQuery is leading serverless warehouse. BigLake for lakehouse patterns with Iceberg/Delta support. BigQuery AI for integrated ML and GenAI.

Data Eng (Ingest, ETL, Streaming).reasoning: Dataflow for streaming/batch (Apache Beam), Dataproc for Spark, Pub/Sub for messaging, Data Fusion for low-code ETL. Comprehensive data engineering.

Orchestration.reasoning: Cloud Composer (managed Airflow) for workflow orchestration, Cloud Workflows for lightweight orchestration, Cloud Scheduler for cron jobs.

BI & Agentic BI.reasoning: Looker for enterprise BI (acquired 2020), Looker Studio for dashboards. Gemini for NL queries. Less mature agentic BI than competitors.

DS/ML.reasoning: Vertex AI with AutoML, custom training on TPUs/GPUs, Feature Store, experiments tracking, and model deployment. BigQuery ML for in-database ML.

Gen AI & Agents Dev.reasoning: Gemini models in Vertex AI, Agent Builder, Agent Development Kit (ADK), Grounding for RAG, fine-tuning support. Google is only platform with video, image, speech, and music models.

Apps Hosting.reasoning: Cloud Run for containers, App Engine for PaaS, Cloud Functions for serverless, GKE for Kubernetes. Comprehensive but not data-platform native hosting.

Open Table Storage.reasoning: BigLake supports Iceberg and Delta but BigQuery's native format is proprietary. Less focus on open formats compared to Databricks.

Catalog & Governance.reasoning: Dataplex for data mesh and governance, Data Catalog for metadata discovery, BigQuery fine-grained access controls. Comprehensive governance layer.

AI Assistants.reasoning: No AI assistants or copilot features across the platform. Traditional interface without modern AI-assisted experiences.

OLTP Databases.reasoning: CDP is for analytics workloads. HBase provides NoSQL but not true OLTP. Customers need separate database solutions.

Data Platform.reasoning: Cloudera Data Platform (CDP) provides unified platform across public cloud, private cloud, and hybrid. Strong for enterprises with on-prem requirements.

DS/ML Platform.reasoning: Cloudera Machine Learning (CML) for ML workloads. Less mature than Databricks MLflow or SageMaker. Limited AutoML and experiment tracking.

GenAI/Agent Platform.reasoning: No native GenAI platform. Relies on partners and integrations for LLM capabilities. Behind competitors in AI platform development.

Data Warehouse/Lakehouse.reasoning: Cloudera Data Warehouse powered by Apache Impala and Hive. Open lakehouse with Iceberg support. Strong for hybrid cloud scenarios.

Data Eng (Ingest, ETL, Streaming).reasoning: NiFi for data ingestion, Spark for processing, Flink for streaming, Kafka included. Comprehensive but requires more operational overhead.

Orchestration.reasoning: Oozie for Hadoop workflow orchestration. Less modern than Airflow or Databricks Workflows. Many customers use external orchestrators.

BI & Agentic BI.reasoning: Data Visualization tool included but limited compared to Power BI or Tableau. No agentic BI capabilities.

DS/ML.reasoning: Cloudera Machine Learning supports model development and deployment. Experiment tracking and Feature Store less mature than competitors.

Gen AI & Agents Dev.reasoning: No native GenAI development capabilities. Customers must integrate external LLM services.

Apps Hosting.reasoning: Can host applications via Kubernetes integration but not a native app development platform. Limited compared to AWS or Azure.

Open Table Storage.reasoning: Strong Iceberg support. Cloudera is major Iceberg contributor. Open Data Lakehouse architecture embraces open formats.

Catalog & Governance.reasoning: Shared Data Experience (SDX) provides comprehensive governance with Atlas-based cataloging, Ranger for security, lineage tracking.

AI Assistants.reasoning: Ask AI for natural language SQL generation. Limited AI assistance compared to modern platforms with full copilot experiences.

OLTP Databases.reasoning: Teradata is OLAP only. Designed for analytics, not transactional workloads.

Data Platform.reasoning: VantageCloud provides enterprise data platform but focused on analytics. Strong warehouse heritage but limited modern data engineering.

DS/ML Platform.reasoning: ClearScape Analytics for in-database ML. BYOM (Bring Your Own Model) for external models. Less comprehensive than dedicated ML platforms.

GenAI/Agent Platform.reasoning: No native GenAI platform. Ask AI features for NL queries but no LLM training or agent framework.

Data Warehouse/Lakehouse.reasoning: Industry pioneer in enterprise data warehousing. VantageCloud Lake for lakehouse patterns. Excellent for large-scale analytics workloads.

Data Eng (Ingest, ETL, Streaming).reasoning: QueryGrid for data federation. Limited native ETL—relies on partners. No native streaming—batch-focused architecture.

Orchestration.reasoning: Basic workflow capabilities. Enterprise customers typically use external orchestration tools like Airflow.

BI & Agentic BI.reasoning: No native BI tool—partners with Tableau, Power BI. Ask AI provides some agentic query capabilities.

DS/ML.reasoning: ClearScape Analytics provides in-database ML with R and Python. Model deployment available. Less feature-rich than dedicated ML platforms.

Gen AI & Agents Dev.reasoning: No GenAI development platform. Limited to Ask AI for query assistance. No LLM serving or agent capabilities.

Apps Hosting.reasoning: Not an application platform. Teradata is purely analytics infrastructure.

Open Table Storage.reasoning: Proprietary storage format. VantageCloud Lake can query open formats but storage remains proprietary.

Catalog & Governance.reasoning: Data Dictionary and access controls. Less comprehensive governance than modern data platforms. QueryGrid provides some federation governance.

AI Assistants.reasoning: AIP assistants within Foundry. Natural language interaction with data and ontology. Less broadly integrated than Microsoft or Google copilots.

OLTP Databases.reasoning: Foundry is for analytics and operations, not transactional databases.

Data Platform.reasoning: Foundry provides unified platform for data integration, transformation, and analysis. Strong for complex enterprise data scenarios and government contracts.

DS/ML Platform.reasoning: ML capabilities within Foundry for model development. Less open than MLflow-based platforms. Proprietary approach to ML lifecycle.

GenAI/Agent Platform.reasoning: AIP (Artificial Intelligence Platform) for enterprise GenAI with LLM integration, ontology-based AI applications, and agent capabilities.

Data Warehouse/Lakehouse.reasoning: Foundry provides warehouse-like capabilities with strong data modeling via Ontology. Good for complex analytical workloads.

Data Eng (Ingest, ETL, Streaming).reasoning: Strong data integration with 200+ connectors. Pipeline Builder for transformations. Real-time data sync capabilities.

Orchestration.reasoning: Built-in workflow and pipeline orchestration in Foundry. Actions for operational workflows that integrate with external systems.

BI & Agentic BI.reasoning: Dashboards and reports in Foundry. Not a dedicated BI tool. AIP provides some agentic capabilities for data exploration.

DS/ML.reasoning: Model training and deployment in Foundry. Code Workbook for development. Less open ecosystem than Databricks.

Gen AI & Agents Dev.reasoning: AIP provides LLM integration with enterprise grounding via Ontology. Logic for AI reasoning workflows. Strong for enterprise AI applications.

Apps Hosting.reasoning: Operational applications can be built in Foundry. Less flexible than dedicated PaaS for custom application development.

Open Table Storage.reasoning: Proprietary data storage. Foundry can connect to external data but uses proprietary formats internally.

Catalog & Governance.reasoning: Strong governance with Ontology providing semantic layer. Fine-grained access control, lineage, and audit capabilities.
